info.name: PulseGuard Control API
info.description:
Every endpoint of the PulseGuard Control API (Stage 3 — Authentication and Project Management).

SETUP
1. Start the API:  cd backend/control-api && ./mvnw spring-boot:run
2. Import this collection into Postman.
3. Run the folders IN ORDER — later requests use tokens and ids captured by earlier ones.

Every request asserts its expected status code, so 'Run collection' gives a pass/fail report. Folder 11 is optional and needs a manual SQL update first.

baseUrl defaults to http://localhost:8080.

item.name: 0 · Public endpoints
item.description: Reachable with no token at all.

exec: pm.test("names the app", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().application).to.eql("PulseGuard Control API"); });

request.description: Only 'health' is exposed and public. Everything else under /actuator falls into anyRequest().authenticated(), so it answers 401 before it would even reach the 'no such endpoint' path — the response does not reveal whether the endpoint exists.

item.name: 1 · Registration
item.description: Creating accounts, and every way it should fail.

request.description: Email is deliberately padded and upper-cased. The response must come back normalized to owner@example.com and the display name trimmed.

exec: pm.test("no password hash in the response", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include("bcrypt"); pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.not.have.property("passwordHash"); });

request.description: RegisterRequest has no systemRole field, so the extra property cannot escalate anything. Whether it is ignored (201) or rejected (400), the account must never come back as ADMIN.

exec: pm.test("never returns an ADMIN account", function () { if (pm.response.code === 201) { pm.expect(pm.response.json().systemRole).to.eql("USER"); } else { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.eql(400); } });

item.name: 2 · Login
item.description: Tokens in, and the failures that must be indistinguishable.

exec: pm.test("body is the generic message", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql("Invalid email or password"); });

request.description: Must be byte-for-byte the same answer as a wrong password, otherwise this endpoint reveals which addresses are registered.

exec: pm.test("body is the generic message", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql("Invalid email or password"); });

request.description: Mixed case on purpose: normalization must let this through. Captures ownerToken for later requests.

exec: pm.test("token has three JWT parts", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().accessToken.split(".")).to.have.lengthOf(3); });
pm.test("no refresh token is issued", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.not.have.property("refreshToken"); });
pm.test("sub is the user id", function () { pm.expect(claims.sub).to.eql(String(pm.response.json().user.id)); });

pm.test("no password data in the token", function () { pm.expect(claims).to.not.have.property("password"); pm.expect(claims).to.not.have.property("passwordHash"); pm.expect(claims).to.not.have.property("password_hash"); });

item.name: 3 · Current user
item.description: Identity is taken from the token, never the request.

exec: pm.test("answers with JSON, not an HTML login page", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get("Content-Type")).to.include("application/json"); });
pm.test("never exposes the password hash", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.not.have.property("passwordHash"); });

item.name: 4 · Projects
item.description: CRUD, plus the isolation between different users.

request.description: The creator automatically becomes PROJECT_ADMIN. Captures projectId.

exec: pm.test("creator is a summary, not the whole user entity", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().createdBy).to.not.have.property("passwordHash"); });
pm.test("contains the new project", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().map(function (p) { return p.name; })).to.include("Production APIs"); });

item.name: Viewer lists projects (not a member yet)

request.description: Must be empty. A user only ever sees projects they belong to.

item.name: Viewer reads the project (not a member yet)

request.description: 404, deliberately NOT 403 — a non-member must not be able to confirm that the project exists.

item.name: Project id that does not exist
5 · Project members
item.description: Adding people who already have an account.

request.description: Exactly one member so far: the creator, as PROJECT_ADMIN.

exec: pm.test("creator is the sole PROJECT_ADMIN", function () { var m = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(m).to.have.lengthOf(1); pm.expect(m[0].role).to.eql("PROJECT_ADMIN"); pm.expect(m[0].email).to.eql("owner@example.com"); });

request.description: Users are never created implicitly — no invitations in this stage.

exec: pm.test("rejected as a bad request", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([400, 422]); });

item.name: 6 · What a VIEWER may and may not do
item.description: Run folder 5 first so the viewer is actually a member.

request.description: 200 now — the same request returned 404 before they joined.
403 rather than 404: a member already knows the project exists.

item.name: 7 · The last-admin rule
item.description: A project must always keep at least one PROJECT_ADMIN. Run in order.

request.description: There are now two admins.
Allowed, because another admin remains. The creator holds no permanent special status.

item.name: Owner is now only a VIEWER
The promoted user can now manage

request.description: Protected again — the rule follows whoever currently holds the role.

item.name: 7b · Monitors
item.description: Monitor configuration. Task 04 stores and validates configuration only — no HTTP health check is ever performed. Run after folder 7, which leaves the viewer as the project's PROJECT_ADMIN and the owner as a VIEWER.

request.description: Run as the project's current PROJECT_ADMIN. Captures monitorId.

exec: pm.test("belongs to the project in the path", function () { pm.expect(String(pm.response.json().projectId)).to.eql(String(pm.collectionVariables.get("projectId"))); });
pm.test("already due, so the future worker will pick it up", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().nextCheckAt).to.not.be.null; });
pm.test("contains the new monitor", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().map(function (m) { return m.name; })).to.include("Payment API"); });

item.name: A monitor id that does not exist

request.description: Configuration only. Operational fields must be untouched.

exec: pm.test("status not altered by a config change", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().currentStatus).to.eql("UNKNOWN"); });
pm.test("still in the same project", function () { pm.expect(String(pm.response.json().projectId)).to.eql(String(pm.collectionVariables.get("projectId"))); });

item.name: Update cannot move the monitor to another project

request.description: The extra fields have no counterpart in UpdateMonitorRequest and are ignored — a client cannot reassign a monitor or assert health.

exec: pm.test("cannot be forced to UP", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().currentStatus).to.eql("UNKNOWN"); });

request.description: UNKNOWN rather than UP: no check has run, so health is genuinely unknown.

exec: pm.test("back to UNKNOWN, not UP", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().currentStatus).to.eql("UNKNOWN"); });

request.description: Only PAUSED monitors transition, so this cannot discard a real state.

item.name: Reject a timeout that outlasts the interval

request.description: A cross-field rule, so it is raised by the service rather than an annotation.
Only GET is supported, so anything else fails to parse — 400, never 500.

item.name: Reject nonsense in the HTTP method

request.description: The owner was demoted to VIEWER in folder 7.

item.name: A VIEWER may read a monitor
7c · Monitoring & Dashboard
item.description: Read-only reporting over the data the Monitor Worker records. Most figures will be empty unless the worker has actually run against these monitors — the assertions are written to pass either way.

request.description: Paginated, newest first. Defaults to page 0, size 50.

exec: pm.test("returns a page envelope, not a raw Spring Page", function () { var d = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(d).to.have.all.keys("content","page","size","totalElements","totalPages","first","last"); });
pm.test("defaults to the first page of 50", function () { var d = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(d.page).to.eql(0); pm.expect(d.size).to.eql(50); });

pm.test("newest first", function () { var c = pm.response.json().content; for (var i = 1; i < c.length; i++) { pm.expect(new Date(c[i-1].checkedAt).getTime()).to.be.at.least(new Date(c[i].checkedAt).getTime()); } });
pm.test("every row is a failure", function () { pm.response.json().content.forEach(function (c) { pm.expect(c.outcome).to.eql("FAILURE"); }); });

pm.test("failures without a response carry a null status", function () { pm.response.json().content.forEach(function (c) { if (c.errorType === "DNS_ERROR" || c.errorType === "CONNECTION_ERROR" || c.errorType === "BLOCKED_ADDRESS") { pm.expect(c.httpStatusCode).to.be.null; } }); });

request.description: Both bounds are inclusive ISO-8601 instants.

exec: pm.test("respects the requested page size", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().size).to.eql(5); });

item.name: Reject a page size above the maximum

request.description: Rejected rather than silently clamped, so a client is never left believing it received everything.
With no range this covers all recorded history — unlike the dashboard, which defaults to the last 24 hours.

exec: pm.test("counts add up", function () { var d = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(d.successfulChecks + d.failedChecks).to.eql(d.totalChecks); });
pm.test("uptime is null with no checks, never zero", function () { var d = pm.response.json(); if (d.totalChecks === 0) { pm.expect(d.uptimePercentage).to.be.null; } });

pm.test("uptime matches the counts", function () { var d = pm.response.json(); if (d.totalChecks > 0) { var expected = Math.round(d.successfulChecks / d.totalChecks * 10000) / 100; pm.expect(Math.abs(d.uptimePercentage - expected)).to.be.below(0.02); } });

pm.test("min <= average <= max when timings exist", function () { var d = pm.response.json(); if (d.averageResponseTimeMs !== null) { pm.expect(d.minimumResponseTimeMs).to.be.at.most(d.averageResponseTimeMs); pm.expect(d.maximumResponseTimeMs).to.be.at.least(d.averageResponseTimeMs); } });
pm.test("echoes the requested range", function () { var d = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(d.from).to.not.be.null; pm.expect(d.to).to.not.be.null; });

item.name: Reject a range that ends before it starts

request.description: Never an empty result — an unknown or inaccessible monitor is a 404.
Defaults to the last 24 hours. Status counts are current state and ignore the window; check figures describe the window.

exec: pm.test("status counts add up to the total", function () { var m = pm.response.json().monitors; pm.expect(m.up + m.down + m.unknown + m.paused).to.eql(m.total); });
pm.test("defaults to a 24 hour window", function () { var w = pm.response.json().window; var hours = (new Date(w.to) - new Date(w.from)) / 3600000; pm.expect(Math.round(hours)).to.eql(24); });
pm.test("check counts add up", function () { var c = pm.response.json().checks; pm.expect(c.successful + c.failed).to.eql(c.total); });
pm.test("at most ten recent failures", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().recentFailures.length).to.be.at.most(10); });

pm.test("no incident metrics — they do not exist yet", function () { var d = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(d).to.not.have.property("activeIncidents"); pm.expect(d).to.not.have.property("incidentCount"); });
pm.test("reports the current open incident count", function () { var d = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(d.openIncidents).to.be.a("number"); pm.expect(d.openIncidents).to.be.at.least(0); });
pm.test("uses the window it was given", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().window.from).to.include("2020-01-01"); });
pm.test("reports the current open incident count", function () { var d = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(d.openIncidents).to.be.a("number"); pm.expect(d.openIncidents).to.be.at.least(0); });

item.name: 7d · Incidents
item.description:
Incident history. An incident is one continuous outage, not one failed check, and it is opened and resolved by the Monitor Worker — there is no POST, PUT or DELETE here on purpose.

These requests need the Monitor Worker to have actually taken a monitor down and brought it back. With no outages yet the lists are legitimately empty, and the assertions below still pass.

request.description: Any project member may read. Paginated, newest first, defaults to page 0 size 20.

exec: pm.test("returns a page envelope, not a raw Spring Page", function () { var d = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(d).to.have.all.keys("content","page","size","totalElements","totalPages","first","last"); });
pm.test("defaults to the first page of 20", function () { var d = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(d.page).to.eql(0); pm.expect(d.size).to.eql(20); });

pm.test("newest first", function () { var c = pm.response.json().content; for (var i = 1; i < c.length; i++) { pm.expect(new Date(c[i-1].openedAt).getTime()).to.be.at.least(new Date(c[i].openedAt).getTime()); } });

pm.test("every incident names its monitor", function () { pm.response.json().content.forEach(function (i) { pm.expect(i).to.have.property("monitorName"); pm.expect(i.monitorId).to.be.a("number"); }); });

request.description: Ongoing outages only. This is what the dashboard's Open incidents card links to.

exec: pm.test("only OPEN comes back", function () { pm.response.json().content.forEach(function (i) { pm.expect(i.status).to.eql("OPEN"); }); });

pm.test("an open incident has no resolution", function () { pm.response.json().content.forEach(function (i) { pm.expect(i.resolvedAt).to.eql(null); pm.expect(i.resolutionCheckId).to.eql(null); }); });

request.description: Past outages. Each one must carry both timestamps.

exec: pm.test("only RESOLVED comes back", function () { pm.response.json().content.forEach(function (i) { pm.expect(i.status).to.eql("RESOLVED"); }); });

pm.test("a resolved incident ended after it began", function () { pm.response.json().content.forEach(function (i) { pm.expect(i.resolvedAt).to.not.eql(null); pm.expect(new Date(i.resolvedAt).getTime()).to.be.at.least(new Date(i.openedAt).getTime()); }); });

item.name: List incidents · pagination and date range

request.description: from/to filter on openedAt, using the same time-window rules as check history.

exec: pm.test("the requested page size is honoured", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().size).to.eql(5); });

pm.test("nothing older than the range", function () { var from = new Date("2020-01-01T00:00:00Z").getTime(); pm.response.json().content.forEach(function (i) { pm.expect(new Date(i.openedAt).getTime()).to.be.at.least(from); }); });

item.name: List incidents · size above the maximum is rejected

request.description: Rejected rather than clamped, so a client is never left believing it received everything.
One incident by its own id. Skipped automatically when no outage has happened yet.

exec: if (!pm.collectionVariables.get("incidentId")) { pm.test.skip("no incident recorded yet", function () {}); } else {

pm.test("carries its monitor and project", function () { var d = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(d.monitorId).to.be.a("number"); pm.expect(d.monitorName).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(d.projectId).to.be.a("number"); });
pm.test("status is OPEN or RESOLVED", function () { pm.expect(["OPEN","RESOLVED"]).to.include(pm.response.json().status); });

request.description: Access is inherited from the monitor's project. A non-member sees 404, never 403.
Identical to the response a non-member gets, so incident ids reveal nothing.

item.name: Incidents are system-generated · POST is refused

request.description: There is no way to declare an outage by hand. Only an observed check can open one.

item.name: 8 · Cross-project isolation
item.description: A membership id from one project must not be reachable through another.

item.name: Change project 1's member via project 2's URL
Delete project 1's member via project 2's URL
9 · CORS
item.description: Browser-enforced. Postman is not a browser, so these only check the headers the server sends back.

exec: pm.test("allows exactly our origin, not a wildcard", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get("Access-Control-Allow-Origin")).to.eql("http://localhost:5173"); });

request.description: Kept alive until now so the reporting folder had something to read.
Its memberships are removed by the database cascade.

item.name: 11 · System ADMIN (optional)
item.description: Registration can never create an ADMIN. Promote one directly in MySQL first:  UPDATE users SET system_role='ADMIN' WHERE email='sneaky@example.com';

item.name: Log in as the promoted admin

request.description: Skips itself if the SQL promotion has not been run, so a plain collection run stays green.

exec: console.log("Skipped: run the SQL promotion first, then re-run folder 11.");

request.description: The admin is a member of nothing, yet sees everything.

exec: pm.test("sees projects without being a member", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.be.an("array"); });
